presentation.label: IMPROVED SMPL
presentation.summary: The SAMPLE page, improved: TUN in cents, FIN's knob as RATE (to a stop and into reverse), LOP PIPO for ping-pong loops, FUNC + STA or END to zero crossings, and SMPL always shows the waveform under one row of values.
presentation.overview: Improved SMPL improves the Rytm's SAMPLE page. TUN turns 1 cent a step, faster as you spin it; press and turn for whole semitones, which keep the cents. The value reads with two places, as LFO depth does: +3.07, +3.00. The cents are kept in TUN itself, so a saved sound plays the same pitch on stock OS, which only shows the whole number. FIN's knob is RATE on every sound, a pure speed control: +63 plays at normal speed, 0 stops, -64 plays backward at normal speed, in a straight line between them, as the Octatrack's RATE with its setting on PTCH. Stock's pitch stops at a quarter of the speed. A trig below 0 starts from END. RATE starts at +63 on a new or cleared sound; a sound saved with FIN at +0 (stock's default, and every sound saved before 0.3.0) loads stopped: turn RATE up to +63. The SMPL key always opens the waveform view (SMPL WAVEFORM); the knob-only view is gone. Its idle screen shows values, not names: TUN, RATE, BR, LOOP (OFF, ON or PIPO) and LEV in one row over a taller waveform. STA and END show as their lines, and turning D opens stock's sample list; the header names whichever knob turns. LOP gets a third value, PIPO, after OFF and ON: the loop between STA and END plays forward, then backward, then forward again, for as long as the note lasts, with each turn exactly on STA or END and no jump. PIPO is an ordinary LOP value: it saves with the sound and kit, takes parameter and scene locks, and plays as ON on an OS without the mod. FUNC + turn on STA or END moves that point to the next zero crossing of the sample the way you turn, stepping as LOP steps; plain turns stay stock. On the waveform a boxed S marks STA's line and a boxed E END's. PIPO and the zero snap came from Ping Pong Loop, which now lives here.
highlights: Tune a sample in cents: turn TUN, press and turn for semitones; it saves in the sound and plays the same on stock OS.
Slow a sample to a dead stop and run it backward from FIN's knob, now RATE on every sound.
Exactly the Octatrack's range: +63 is 1x, 0 stops, -64 is -1x.
SMPL always shows the waveform, taller, under one row of values: TUN, RATE, BR, LOOP, LEV.
Ping-pong loops from LOP's third value, PIPO: lock it on a step or put it in a scene; no jump at the turns.
FUNC + STA or END steps through the sample's zero crossings, for click-free start and loop points.
Ping Pong Loop now lives here: one module for how a sample plays from the SAMPLE page.
usage: Press SMPL and turn TUN slowly: it moves 1 cent a step and reads +0.01, +0.02. Spin it faster to cover more ground.
Press TUN's knob and turn: whole semitones, the cents kept.
Put a long sample on a track, with LOP ON, and set RATE (FIN's knob) to +63. Play the pad and turn RATE down: the sample slows like a stopping turntable and rests at 0.
Keep turning below 0: it runs backward, smoothly through the stop. A new trig now starts from END.
Turn LOP (knob G) past ON to PIPO and play the sound: the loop between STA and END goes back and forth. Set them around a sustained part (a pad, a vowel) for a seamless drone.
Hold FUNC and turn STA (or END): the point steps from zero crossing to zero crossing, so the loop starts and ends where the waveform crosses zero.

access.location: SAMPLE page (SMPL key, always the waveform view): TUN (A) in cents, RATE (B, FIN's knob), LOP (G) OFF, ON or PIPO, FUNC + STA (E) or END (F) to zero crossings.
steps: Select a track whose sound plays a sample, and press SMPL: the waveform view opens.
Turn encoder A (TUN) for cents; press and turn it for semitones.
Turn encoder B (RATE): +63 is normal speed, 0 stops, below 0 plays backward.
Turn encoder G (LOP) clockwise past ON: the value reads PIPO.
Hold FUNC and turn encoder E (STA) or F (END): the point steps from zero crossing to zero crossing.

controls.name: TUN
controls.doc: SAMPLE page, encoder A. -24.00 to +24.00 semitones. A plain turn moves 1 cent a step, with acceleration; press and turn moves whole semitones and keeps the cents. FUNC + turn jumps -24, 0, +24 as stock. Held trigs' locks take cents the same way. The value reads with two places, as LFO depth: +3.07, +3.00, and (0) at zero.

controls.name: RATE
controls.doc: SAMPLE page, encoder B (FIN's knob), on every sound. +63 to -64: speed scales by |RATE| / 64, backward below 0, and +63 is exactly 1x. Starts at +63 on a new or cleared sound. TUN still multiplies it. Locks, LFOs and MIDI CC 25 reach it.

controls.name: LOP
controls.doc: SAMPLE page, encoder G. OFF and ON as stock; PIPO plays the loop between STA and END forward, then backward, and so on. Locks per step and per scene. The value row reads OFF, ON or PIPO; where stock draws LOP's switch (the knob view, if another module brings it back), it has three positions, as BD CLASSIC's WAV: OFF left, ON middle, PIPO right.

controls.name: FUNC + STA / END
controls.doc: SAMPLE page, FUNC held, encoder E or F: STA or END steps to the next zero crossing the way you turn, as often as LOP would step a value (more on a fast turn), the frame stock plays from; with none further it holds. STA and END may pass each other or share a crossing. With LOP ON only crossings of the other point's direction. With a trig held in GRID RECORDING it steps that trig's lock. Exact up to 30,720 frames (0.64 s); longer samples take the nearest step. Plain turns are stock.

controls.name: SMPL key
controls.doc: Opens the SAMPLE page in its waveform view (SMPL WAVEFORM) every time; a second press stays there. One row of values over a taller waveform: TUN, RATE, BR, LOOP (OFF, ON or PIPO) and LEV, where knobs A, B, C, G and H turn them. STA and END (E, F) show as their lines and D opens the sample list, as stock. While a knob turns, the header names it.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, with core-ar2 0.7.

Since 0.6.0 Improved SMPL 0.5.1 and Ping Pong Loop 0.1.2 are one module, code unchanged; Ping Pong Loop has left the library. Run on a unit as MSU1 (rig and author). Not run on a unit: several voices in PIPO, a scene lock of PIPO, MIDI CC 30 by ear, samples over 0.64 s, RATE on two voices, scene and performance locks on RATE, a sound browser load. TESTING.md has the rest.

The waveform view shows no text for STA, END and SMP: STA and END show as their lines, D's sample list as on stock. With a trig held, a lock on STA, END or SMP gets no box; locks on the row's five are boxed there.
The SAMPLE page's knob-only view is not shown. If another module adds a page behind the SMPL key, the knob view stays in the cycle.

A sound saved with FIN at +0 (stock's default, and every sound saved before 0.3.0 without SMP RATE) loads with RATE 0: the sample does not play until RATE is turned up. On stock OS a sound saved with RATE +63 plays about a semitone sharp (FIN as a detune).

MIDI CC 24 sets TUN in whole semitones and clears its cents, as stock's CC does; NRPN keeps them to 1/128 semitone; other screens (LFO destinations, a sound lock's list) and stock OS show TUN as a whole number.
A pattern with TUN locks in cents saves one more lock lane per track, of stock's 72; stock OS loads those locks with their cents.
RATE never goes above 1x by itself (TUN does, to stock's ceiling of about 4x). With LOP OFF, once the sample has played out, changing RATE does not bring it back: trig again.
A change of direction on a looping voice waits until it is 32 frames clear of STA and END; a trig does not wait.

A sample previewed with FUNC + YES in a sample list plays at 1x, as on stock, whatever the track's RATE or an LFO on it: stock plays a preview from its own slot 129, and the module plays any voice on a slot of 128 or above at 1x, forward.
Sound locks, scene locks and performance locks on RATE have not been run.

Zero snap is exact only on samples up to 30,720 frames (0.64 s at 48 kHz): STA and END are steps of 1/30,720 of the sample, so on longer samples the point lands on the nearest step, up to frames / 61,440 frames from the crossing (1 frame at 1 s, about 8 at 10 s, 47 at 60 s).
MIDI CC 30 (LOP) writes its value unchanged, as on stock: CC value 2 now gives PIPO, every other nonzero value ON. Other OFF/ON parameters still read ON for 2.
On stock OS, or a build without this mod, PIPO plays as ON; LOP reads ERROR for it until the knob is turned, which steps between OFF and ON.
LOP's switch is drawn with the knob in the middle for ON, where stock draws it on the right; the value text still reads ON.
FUNC + turn on STA or END no longer gives stock's whole-number steps; use a plain turn for fine moves. A very slow FUNC turn registers no change, as on LOP and stock's stepped controls.
With END on the sample's very last frame, a turn can land up to 7 frames off (rytm-emu: the first turn after a hit); set END a little before the end for exact turns.

Exact turns depend on DMA reading frames the module writes (every cache way is pushed first); rytm-emu does not model the cache; PIPO played on the author's unit, and a dedicated click check of the turns on a unit is still open.
While a FUNC turn settles (stock glides STA and END over a fraction of a second), a loop wrap or PIPO turn can click; settled points are clean.
On SMPL WAVEFORM a STA or END line can sit one column left of its crossing (stock spaces the lines over 123 columns and the waveform over 124); the frame played is the crossing.

claims: param:FIN (id 40) is RATE: its names read RATE and its default is +63
param:TUN (id 39) turn and value text: fine in cents
screen:SAMPLE knob page (the SMPL key shows SMPL WAVEFORM only)
screen:SMPL WAVEFORM layout: one value row and a taller waveform
ui:SAMPLE page LOP value PIPO and its three-position switch
param:LOP range OFF/ON/PIPO, its value text and icon
ui:FUNC + SAMPLE STA/END turn with a trig held
ui:SMPL WAVEFORM S and E labels on the STA and END lines

load.display: Near nothing for RATE while no track's RATE is below 0; PIPO about as Ping Pong Loop 0.1.2 (measured with it)
load.conditions: Measured on an Analog Rytm MKII with a private telemetry base, sequencer stopped, in the author's 16-module set (RC30): removing Sample Playback Rate 0.1.0 lowered the idle block from 72.9 % to 72.1 %, removing Ping Pong Loop 0.1.1 to 70.6 %; with both idle fixes (LF01), 71.1 %. Since then RATE's handler returns at once while no track's RATE is below 0, and PIPO tests one byte of armed voices before its gates' work. 0.6.0 is the same code, unmeasured. Since 0.6.3 PIPO's follower returns early while no voice is in PIPO (rytm-emu: 110 to 164 fewer instructions a block).

hardware.summary: 0.6.2 ran on npp1993's Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74, as SU62 (the author's development base with the link + this module only, sha256 886783f3…6678), booted from RAM over the flashed CM02 in a scratch project: the rig's rest case passed all 30 checks (the follower's rest byte set with LOP OFF on every track and cleared by LOP ON or PIPO; PIPO armed and turning, also right after a rest), and the earlier cases' screens read as before. 0.6.0 ran as MSU1 the same way: the rig's twelve cases with no failed check, and by hand the author reports all pass: the waveform view and row; PIPO back and forth with no click at the turns; FUNC + STA and END to zero crossings with the S and E labels; RATE through 0 into reverse with LOP ON and PIPO; TUN in cents and semitones; a PIPO lock on a held trig. 0.6.1 links to the same image as 0.6.0.
limitations: Hand results are reported by the author from playing; the rig's twelve cases are its own checks, five of them without stored references (judged by eye).
The image holds the author's private development base (with the link), not the published base.
0.6.2 and 0.6.3 ran on the unit under the rig only: nothing of them was played or heard by hand; their CPU saving is an emulator count.

Not run on a unit: several voices in PIPO at once, a scene lock of PIPO, MIDI CC 30 by ear, samples over 0.64 s, a power cycle with PIPO saved, sound browser load, scene and performance locks on RATE.

tests.summary: Unit (0.6.2, SU62 from RAM): the rig's rest case, 30 checks passed. Unit (0.6.0, MSU1 from RAM): the rig's 12 cases with no failed check; by hand, as the author reports, PIPO, zero snap and labels, RATE through 0 with ON and PIPO, TUN, a PIPO lock. rytm-emu: 0.6.2 against 0.6.1, identical state and audio over 144,552 blocks; (MS01) every documented capture of Ping Pong Loop and Improved SMPL replays byte-identical to the two side by side (126 frames). Earlier versions and Ping Pong Loop's history: TESTING.md.
